v.q: What runs first when the call stack empties?
v.w: The event loop drains the microtask queue before it takes the next task.

v.q: Why can a long loop freeze a web page?
o: It keeps the only thread busy
v.w: Nothing can interrupt a running function, so clicks, timers and rendering wait.

v.q: In what order do synchronous code, a promise callback and setTimeout(0) run?
v.w: Microtasks run before the next task, and a zero delay is still a task.

v.q: When does the function passed to new Promise run?
v.w: Only the then callbacks are asynchronous. The executor runs at once.
That is why calls chain, and a returned promise is awaited before the next step.

v.q: How many times can a promise settle?
v.w: After it is fulfilled or rejected it never changes again.

v.q: Which helper reports every outcome and never rejects?
v.w: Each result is an object with status and value or reason.

v.q: What does Promise.any do when every promise rejects?
v.w: It fulfills with the first success, so it rejects only when there is none.
The rest of the program keeps running while the function waits.

v.q: Why is await inside forEach a bug?
o: It makes the loop run twice
v.w: Use for...of for sequence, or Promise.all with map for parallel work.

v.q: Three independent one-second calls are awaited one after another. How long do they take?
v.w: Awaiting each in turn adds the times. Promise.all would take about one second.

v.q: Which approach runs independent calls in parallel?
v.w: Start them first, then wait for all at once.
An HTTP error status still resolves, so check res.ok.

v.q: How do you cancel a fetch request?
v.w: Pass its signal to fetch and call abort. Promises themselves cannot be cancelled.

v.q: What does Node.js do by default on an unhandled rejection since version 15?
v.w: A missing catch can crash a server, so handle or return every promise.
Workers have their own thread, so the main event loop stays responsive.
